claim: The perturbation reconstructed for the flagged class acts like the attacker's real trigger, so briefly fine-tuning the delivered model on clean labelled images carrying that perturbation removes the backdoor without hurting accuracy, which fine-tuning on clean images or with other perturbations does not. Supported only if, averaged over ten datasets for each of five attacks (including the adaptive one), repair with the reconstructed perturbation brings attack success below 10% with clean accuracy within 1 point of the original, while clean-only fine-tuning, random perturbations and the perturbation from a wrong class each leave average attack success above 40%.

experiments: Set up models, attacks and the detector. Setup: CLIP ViT-B/16 with frozen encoders, prompt-tuned with CoCoOp (two-layer meta-net producing image-conditioned tokens) on the seen classes of ImageNet, Caltech101, OxfordPets, Flowers102, Food101, FGVC, SUN397, DTD, EuroSAT and UCF101 (16-shot unseen evaluation). Attacks poison 10% of tuning images: BadCLIP (dense trigger, epsilon 4/255, jointly optimised with the meta-net), and Blended, WaNet and SIBA adapted to prompt tuning; average backdoor success on unseen classes 69.8-97.6% by dataset. Detector: 50 candidate classes including the target; 1,000 unlabeled Open Images with no class overlap; per class, one epoch (32 Adam steps, lr 0.1, batch 32) minimising the negative margin between the class logit and the strongest other logit under an L-inf bound of 4/255; score = z(held-out success) - z(loss), re-standardised within the model; backdoored if the maximum is at least k = 2. Baselines: Neural Cleanse and Pixel Backdoor with their original losses.

Repair with the reconstructed trigger. Setup: with a small labelled clean set, fine-tune CoCoOp-style on clean images carrying the flagged class's perturbation with their true labels for a few gradient steps; ten datasets per attack. Result: attack success before / after 98.48 / 7.61% (BadCLIP), 64.35 / 4.23% (adaptive), 99.73 / 7.64% (Blended), 66.30 / 5.76% (SIBA), 92.99 / 5.27% (WaNet); clean accuracy 81.76 to 81.35%, 81.62 to 81.04%, 81.69 to 81.69%, 75.91 to 77.93% and 82.08 to 82.11%.

Compare with repair controls. Setup: same fine-tuning on clean images only, with a random perturbation, or with the perturbation reconstructed for a non-target class; averages over all attacks and datasets. Result: attack success after repair 64.6% (clean only), 52.7% (random), 47.0% (wrong class) against 6.1% with the reconstructed target-class trigger, from 84.4% before; accuracy changes within 1 point in all. SIBA is the exception, removed by every control (5.4-8.6%), while WaNet survives random and wrong-class repair (86.5%, 70.0%).
